I didn't find a Long Island-specific revenue figure for residential pool service. The results only give national or regional numbers, so any Long Island estimate would have to be derived from them.

- **National service revenue:** IBISWorld puts the swimming pool cleaning services industry at about $7.2 billion in 2024, growing at a CAGR of 2.8% over the past five years.
- **Conflicting figure:** BlueWeave Consulting estimates the U.S. pool maintenance and cleaning services market at USD 8.69 million in 2024. That is almost certainly a unit error for billions, given IBISWorld's figure, so I'd discount it.
- **Derived direct-service estimate:** A pool industry blog (Pooldial) starts from Leslie's 10-K residential pool aftermarket of $8.4 billion and assumes a 30% direct-service share. That yields roughly a $2.52 billion direct service market, split across about 125,000 service businesses. This is a rough calculation, not a published market size.
- **Regional context:** A Pool & Spa News top-50 service list reports 2023 residential service revenue by region. One block shows about $123.9 million in residential service revenue across 43 locations, but the page doesn't label that region, so I can't attribute it to the Northeast or Long Island.

A Long Island-specific estimate would likely require scaling national or Northeast figures by housing or pool counts, or a paid regional report. The Pooldial piece is the closest to a usable base, but it's a vendor blog that does its own arithmetic.

content.text:
**Use $265 million, but only if you can re-find the bank report and confirm its scope. Don't use $410 million.**

- **$410M has no source.** Your partner can't locate the trade deck, so you can't cite it on a client slide. If he can find it again, or the association's publication, it becomes a candidate.
- **$265M has a source, but you need to confirm it.** Find the bank's report and check three things: whether it covers residential or all pool service, whether the geography is Long Island or Nassau and Suffolk, and whether it counts service revenue or also chemicals and equipment. A gap this size usually comes from one of those differences.
- **I couldn't settle it from public data.** My search found no Long Island residential pool-service revenue figure. The closest public numbers are national: IBISWorld puts pool cleaning services at about [$7.2B in 2024](https://img.ibisworld.com/united-states/industry/swimming-pool-cleaning-services/4832), and a [Pooldial analysis](https://pooldial.com/resources/articles/business/how-many-pools-in-united-states) derives a direct-service share of about $2.5B from Leslie's 10-K. Neither gives a Long Island number.

If you can't recover the bank report in the next day or so, don't put either number on the slide as fact. Build a bottom-up estimate instead: Long Island residential pool count × share under weekly service × average annual service fee. Label each input and its source, and show the range. That will hold up better in front of a client than a number nobody can trace.

Sources:
- [IBISWorld: Swimming Pool Cleaning Services](https://img.ibisworld.com/united-states/industry/swimming-pool-cleaning-services/4832)
- [Pooldial: How many pools in the United States](https://pooldial.com/resources/articles/business/how-many-pools-in-united-states)
- [Pool & Spa News: Top 50 Service List](https://www.poolspanews.com/companies/top-50-service/slicing-and-dicing-this-years-top-50-service-list)
